description: Somos o Cuscuz Galático! Uma equipe paraibana que une tecnologia, ciência, criatividade e inovação para transformar ideias em soluções. Representamos a identidade nordestina no NASA Space Apps Challenge, mostrando que grandes ideias podem nascer em qualquer lugar e alcançar o universo. Do Nordeste para as estrelas!
summary: "Astro Mission" is an immersive, web-based space survival and strategy simulation designed to make aerospace education interactive and engaging. Players take on the role of a lunar colony Commander, tasked with managing vital resources like oxygen, water, and power while upgrading base modules to achieve full self-sufficiency. What sets this simulator apart is its integration of real-world NASA data and historical spaceflight anomalies. Throughout the game, players face critical events—such as the Apollo 13 oxygen tank explosion, Mir station collisions, or DONKI-alerted solar flares—and must make strategic decisions to survive. A built-in robotic assistant, L.U.M.I., provides scientific context for every outcome, bridging the gap between gameplay and real physics. Built with React and featuring a procedural Web Audio API sound engine, the game is lightweight, bilingual (EN/PT), and highly accessible on any device. By transforming complex space hazards into a hands-on, cause-and-effect gaming experience, "Cuscuz Galáctico" actively inspires the next generation of engineers and astronauts to explore the wonders of STEM.
details:
What does it do and how does it work? "Astro Mission" is an interactive aerospace survival simulator that puts players in the shoes of a lunar colony commander. The core gameplay loop revolves around resource management and base expansion. Players gather raw materials (regolith, ice, and mechanical parts) through rover exploration missions and use them to build and upgrade vital life-support modules, such as the Main Habitat, Water Purifier, and Solar Panels. The game features a real-time survival engine that continuously tracks the crew's health, fatigue, and base resources (Oxygen, Water, Food, and Power). If the colony runs out of supplies, the crew faces critical conditions, requiring players to balance exploration, construction, and crew rest periods to achieve a fully self-sufficient colony.

How is your project creative? The true creativity of the project lies in merging survival gaming mechanics with real-world NASA data and historical spaceflight anomalies. Instead of generic sci-fi threats, players face dynamic emergencies directly inspired by actual events—such as the Apollo 13 oxygen tank explosion, Mir station collisions, James Webb telescope deployment jams, and DONKI-alerted solar flares. Players must make tactical choices to resolve these crises. Once a decision is made, the in-game AI assistant, L.U.M.I., provides a scientific report explaining the real-world physics, chemistry, and engineering behind their choice and its consequences.

What benefits does it have and what is the intended impact? The primary benefit is active learning. Instead of passively reading about space hazards, players experience them through engaging cause-and-effect mechanics. The intended impact is to democratize aerospace education, breaking down complex scientific concepts into an entertaining format that inspires young minds (ages 8-13) to pursue STEM careers. By supporting a fully bilingual interface (English and Portuguese) that switches in real-time, we ensure this knowledge is accessible to a broader global audience.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use? We developed the simulator as a lightweight, browser-based application to ensure maximum cross-platform compatibility without requiring heavy downloads.

  • Languages & Frameworks: TypeScript, React, and HTML5/CSS3.
  • State Management: Zustand, which powers the complex, real-time survival loop and inventory persistence.
  • UI & Animations: Tailwind CSS for a responsive layout and Framer Motion for fluid, immersive interface transitions.
  • Audio Engine: Instead of relying on heavy external audio files (.mp3 or .wav), we engineered a custom procedural sound synthesizer using the native Web Audio API. All sound effects—from astronaut thrusters and construction noises to NASA emergency sirens—are generated mathematically through code.

What factors did your team consider? Our team heavily prioritized User Experience (UX) and accessibility. We designed an intuitive, single-screen management panel tailored for younger audiences, preventing cognitive overload by using clear visual feedback, color-coded alerts, and dynamic tutorials. Furthermore, we considered performance and scalability; by utilizing the Web Audio API and modular code architecture, the application runs incredibly fast even on low-end hardware, and the event system is easily scalable to integrate future NASA datasets.
